sources.title: Grok 4.3 model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact model grok-4.3 and alias grok-4.3-latest: text/image input, text output, 1,000,000 context, function calling and configurable reasoning. Defaults to low; none disables reasoning. No model-size or neural-network details are provided.

sources.title: Elon Musk: Grok 4.3 early beta, April 17, 2026
sources.evidence: Direct X embed JSON identifies Elon Musk and timestamp 2026-04-17T23:35:41.000Z. He calls Grok 4.3 an early beta and invites people to try it. Canonical post: https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2045285099680252417. Direct HTML access failed, but this first-party JSON was accessed successfully.

sources.title: Elon Musk: 0.5T checkpoint clarification, April 18, 2026
sources.evidence: Direct X JSON identifies Musk, timestamp 2026-04-18T00:09:39.000Z and reply parent 2045076039928336816. He corrects that the checkpoint is still 0.5T; the larger 1T model is still training. Canonical post: https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2045293644693770630.

sources.title: Parent post explicitly naming Grok 4.3 beta
sources.evidence: The April 17 parent post explicitly names Grok 4.3 beta and SuperGrok Heavy availability. Its claimed 1T parameter size is the assertion Musk corrects in s3; it is not used as technical evidence. Parent and reply IDs establish exact variant context.

sources.title: Aditya Gupta profile and affiliation
sources.evidence: Indexed first-party profile identifies Aditya Gupta as affiliated with xAI. The account joined December 2013. This establishes the affiliation of the author of s5; the exact post JSON supplies the stable account ID despite a later handle change.

sources.title: Chat with Files
sources.evidence: Files attached by input_file automatically enable document-search tools and an agentic workflow. This is a service workflow, not evidence of a separate native PDF input modality.

sources.title: Enterprise Terms, April 10, 2026
sources.evidence: Release-period service terms provide limited API/service access, reserve xAI ownership of underlying technology, and restrict copying/reverse engineering. Supports proprietary classification, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: Public xai-org model repository inventory
sources.evidence: Fresh public organization listing contains grok-1 and grok-2, not Grok 4.3. Combined with hosted API documentation and service terms, no public Grok 4.3 weights are evidenced.

sources.title: Safety and model-card index
sources.evidence: Current index links Grok 4.5, 4.6 and 4.7 cards plus earlier Grok cards, but no Grok 4.3 card. Microsoft prose mentions a Grok 4.3 card without supplying an accessible link; no exact-model card was obtained.

sources.evidence: Complete indexed PDF and cached text checked. Exact Grok 4.3 comparisons appear in GDPval and MTS evaluation figures; they report performance, not total/active parameters or neural-network architecture. No such disclosure for 4.3 found.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 model card, September 21, 2026
sources.evidence: Complete indexed PDF and cached text checked for exact Grok 4.3 references, parameter counts and network structure. No Grok 4.3 specification disclosure found; later sibling specifications are not transferred.

sources.title: Frontier Artificial Intelligence Framework, June 30, 2026

sources.title: Grok Model Retirement on May 15, 2026
sources.evidence: Documents older reasoning/non-reasoning slugs redirecting to grok-4.3 with low/none effort from May 15. Specifies 1M context. This later routing event is not the initial Grok 4.3 release and does not transfer older model specifications.

sources.title: Grok 4.3 partner model documentation
sources.evidence: Lists xAI Grok 4.3 preview on Google Cloud dated May 27, 2026, text/image input, text output, functions and reasoning. Context limit is 200,000 on this provider, not the native xAI 1M limit.

sources.title: Grok 4.3 Microsoft Foundry catalog
sources.evidence: Exact model author xAI, hosted preview, quick facts text/image to text and 200k context. Prose also claims video and always-on reasoning, conflicting with its quick facts and native xAI configurable reasoning; native xAI documentation is used for this record. No actual Grok 4.3 card link was supplied.

sources.title: Grok on Amazon Bedrock, June 17, 2026
sources.evidence: States Grok 4.3 is generally available on Bedrock on June 17, with 1M context and configurable reasoning. This is a later provider rollout, not the model debut.

name.note: Exact display name and grok-4.3 API identifier.

developer.note: xAI is the original developer; current documentation uses the later SpaceXSI branding.

family.note: Normalized family name from the developer model name and identifier.

release_date.note: Earliest public beta availability, explicitly acknowledged by Musk on April 17 UTC. The later API rollout, May 15 alias migration, May 27 Google preview and June 17 Bedrock release are distinct events.

open_weights.note: Documented hosted service; no Grok 4.3 download in the public organization inventory. Earlier Grok-1/Grok-2 weight releases do not apply.

license.note: Descriptive service licensing classification supported by release-period terms; not an SPDX license or a claim of downloadable weights.

parameters_b.note: Nominal approximately 0.5 trillion total model parameters. Musk corrects an explicit Grok 4.3 beta size claim, and xAI researcher Gupta independently states the same approximate size at the API launch. This is a developer-reported rounded count, not a tensor audit; no guarantee for future revisions of a moving alias.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-per-token count in the model page, developer size statements or later exact-model comparison figures. Total parameters do not establish active parameters; no dense/MoE assumption is made.

architecture.note: No neural-network architecture disclosed for this exact model in the accessed documentation/cards. Exact-model training and interpretability searches found no primary architecture disclosure. Multi-agent product behavior and sibling designs are not neural architecture evidence.

context_window.note: Native xAI API context. Google and Microsoft provider limits are 200k; those do not overwrite the native 1M setting. A commercial long-context pricing threshold at 200k is not a 200k native maximum.

modalities.note: Native documented model modalities. Remove PDF: file attachments use document-search tools. Conflicting Microsoft narrative video claims are not adopted over native documentation and its own text/image quick facts; generated office files are service outputs.

reasoning.note: Configurable reasoning, including none and low/medium/high; low default. Current detailed table additionally lists xhigh. No always-on assertion is made.

description.value: Grok model with configurable reasoning, text and image input, tool calling, and a one-million-token context window.
description.note: Replace temporary default-model positioning and comparative hallucination claims with documented capabilities.

patch.description: Grok model with configurable reasoning, text and image input, tool calling, and a one-million-token context window.
patch.notes: April 17, 2026 is the public beta date. Approximately 500B total parameters is a rounded developer-reported size: Musk clarified the beta checkpoint on April 18 and xAI researcher Aditya Gupta corroborated it at the API launch on May 1. Active parameters and neural-network architecture remain undisclosed in the sources reviewed. Native xAI context is 1M; Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry document 200k limits. PDF attachments use document-search tools. May 15 redirects from older model slugs do not change this model's release date.

summary: Confirmed April 17 public beta from first-party X data and native 1M context, text/image inputs, reasoning and function calling. Added nominal 500B total parameters from independently accessed Musk and xAI-researcher statements, plus proprietary licensing. Removed PDF native-input claim and unsupported comparative/default-model description. Active count and network architecture remain undisclosed after later-card and exact-model research checks; no sibling or redirect specifications were transferred.
